meta.title: Cloud-native e-commerce platform
meta.subtitle: Container level: three services, one gateway, joined by events

dr.backup_strategy: Replica in a second zone; five-minute log shipping
Synchronous replica in a second zone; continuous backup

cards.title: Request path
items: Every call enters through the gateway, which validates the token and applies limits
Nine calls in ten browse the catalog; one in ten reaches checkout
Each service owns its data: no service reads another service's store

cards.title: Events
items: Checkout publishes "order placed" from a transactional outbox
Fulfilment and the catalog consume it; every consumer is idempotent
A slow consumer builds lag on the stream and does not slow checkout

cards.title: Levels
items: This is the container level of the C4 model
Catalog, checkout and fulfilment each open into a component diagram
Each level has its own figures, review and failure scenarios

cards.title: Assumptions
items: Every figure in this example is an illustrative design target, not a vendor commitment or a measurement
The whole platform runs in one region: a regional outage stops the shop
The gateway keeps answering when a service behind it fails, with that feature missing

adrs.title: One region with three zones
adrs.context: The shop sells in one market. A second region would double the data stores and require conflict handling for orders and stock.
adrs.decision: Run in one region across three zones, with every store replicated to a second zone, and rehearse a restore into another region.

cons: Stock and orders need conflict resolution

adrs.consequences: A regional outage stops the shop until the restore completes. The failure scenario for a region shows this plainly.

adrs.title: Events are published from a transactional outbox
adrs.context: An order that is stored but never announced is never shipped; an order that is announced but not stored is shipped without a record.
adrs.decision: Write the order and its event in one database transaction, and let a relay publish the outbox to the event stream.

alternatives.option: Write to the store, then publish
cons: A crash between the two steps loses or invents an order

adrs.consequences: Events can be delivered more than once, so every consumer must be idempotent. They are.

alternatives.title: Checkout capped at 5 instances
alternatives.description: A lower autoscaling ceiling to reduce peak spend

meta.title: Inside the catalog service
meta.subtitle: Component level: browsing and search read from fresh copies

dr.backup_strategy: Replica in a second zone; five-minute log shipping

cards.title: What is inside
items: The API answers browsing from the product reader and search from the index
The product reader reads through a cache in front of the catalog store
The indexer applies stock and price events to the search index

cards.title: Staleness
items: Search results lag the catalog store by the time the indexer takes
If search fails, browsing still works: the call sits behind a circuit breaker
The index can be rebuilt from the catalog store

cards.title: Assumptions
items: Every figure in this example is an illustrative design target, not a vendor commitment or a measurement
Entry load is the share of platform traffic that reaches the catalog

meta.title: Inside the checkout service
meta.subtitle: Component level: one order, paid for and recorded exactly once

dr.backup_strategy: Synchronous replica in a second zone; continuous backup

cards.title: What is inside
items: The API validates the request and splits it: cart changes or an order
The order workflow owns the saga: authorise, record, publish
The payment adapter is the only component that talks to the provider

cards.title: Exactly once
items: The order and its event are written in one transaction
A relay publishes the outbox to the event stream, and may publish twice
Every payment call carries an idempotency key

cards.title: Assumptions
items: Every figure in this example is an illustrative design target, not a vendor commitment or a measurement
Entry load is the share of platform traffic that reaches checkout

meta.title: Inside the fulfilment service
meta.subtitle: Component level: an order becomes a stock hold and a shipment

dr.backup_strategy: Synchronous replica in a second zone

cards.title: What is inside
items: One consumer reads order placed events in order, per order
It reserves stock, plans the shipment and asks for a customer message
A message that keeps failing is parked in dead letters, not retried forever

cards.title: Failure handling
items: Every step is idempotent: an event delivered twice has one effect
The carrier and the message provider sit behind circuit breakers
A slow carrier delays the shipment, never the order

cards.title: Assumptions
items: Every figure in this example is an illustrative design target, not a vendor commitment or a measurement
Entry load is the rate of orders placed on the platform
